Container.Name: isputnik
Container.Overview:
Private self-hosted family media library, now in Beta (4.0.0 and later). Audiobooks with a built-in player, ebooks with an in-browser reader, and a photo and video gallery with face recognition (the isputnik-faces container beside it, nothing leaves your server), albums, slideshows rendered to MP4, and a Photo Inbox for scans and photos from relatives. The family writes its own stories and recipes around what the house holds, and keeps a family tree linked to the people found in the photos. Multiple accounts with per-person progress and permissions, sharing and guest links, passkeys and two-factor sign-in, an installable PWA with offline listening, and an English or Russian interface.
Beta means your data is looked after: the database migrates itself forward on every upgrade, a copy of it is saved before each new version starts, and backups can be scheduled from the Control panel. Features are still moving. On first run, open the web UI on your home network to create the administrator account.
Container.Changes:
### 2026.11.13 — 4.89.1 A damaged ebook no longer stops the scan - **One damaged EPUB no longer stops the whole ebook library scan.** A book whose zip was broken ("Invalid CEN header") opened without complaint and failed only when the scanner read the first file inside it, where nothing caught the error: the scan stopped, every retry hit the same book, and the library ended on **scan error**. A book that can't be read is now added with its title taken from its file name and no cover, and any other error in a single book is logged and skipped, so one book can never stop the scan again. Thanks to Stefan Knol for tracking it down.
### 2026.11.12 — 4.89.0 Diagnostics for bug reports - **A diagnostics report to attach to a bug report.** Control panel › Infrastructure › Diagnostics puts together what a bug report needs, so nobody has to ask what you are running: this server's version and machine, the containers beside it and whether they answer, the libraries and their scan state, the failures in the activity log over the last two weeks, and what each container says about itself. The video container (0.38.0 or later) adds its ffmpeg, what its GPU check found and the GPU's recent failures, its conversion settings and the warnings and errors in its log. **Copy report** and **Download .txt** take it, and **Open a bug report** opens the form with your version filled in. - **It keeps your family's details out unless you ask.** People's names and emails, library names, folders, file names, IP addresses and web addresses are replaced with `<person>`, `<name>`, `<path>`, `<ip>` and `<host>` until you turn on **Include names, folders and addresses**, which warns that bug reports on GitHub are public. Every part can be left out, the whole report is shown before you copy it, and nothing is sent anywhere by the app. The bug report form now asks for it. - **The video cache in the guide.** The Video guide covers the cache settings from 4.88.0 (where conversions are made, Keep ready, when downloads are prepared), with screenshots, and the control panel search finds them.
### 2026.11.12 — 4.88.0 Video kept ready, downloads on your terms - **Converted video starts in memory.** Films a browser can't play as they are are converted in memory first, and on a disk only once the video container has one of its own. Settings › Video › Converting video shows the fast disk and its free space, or says there is none and how to map one, and offers memory only, memory then the disk, or the disk only, with one memory limit for everyone. Before, an empty Transcode folder on Unraid quietly wrote conversions and copies for download inside the container. Needs the video container 0.35. - **Watched together, converted once.** Two people watching the same film at the same quality share one conversion, and the second one doesn't take a place from the household's limit. Converting video marks who is watching together. - **Films kept after watching.** A film that had to be converted is kept once someone has watched it to the end, so it plays next time with nothing converted; one left mostly watched is finished off in the background. Kept films and copies for download share one room (Room for kept video, 50 GB to start with), listed on Settings › Copies for download. - **Keep ready.** An admin can keep a film, a show or one season ready from its More menu: converted ahead of time at 1080p, 720p or 480p and never removed to make room, with a show's new episodes following. Titles kept ready are listed beside the copies, with how far each has got. - **When downloads are prepared.** A new page under Settings › Video sets when the video app does its background work — right away, when the server is idle, or only at night — how many jobs at once, how many downloads one member may have waiting, and a download speed for copies going away from home. The queue is shown there, with Run now, Move to the top and Take off the queue. A download waiting to be prepared says whether it waits for the night or a quiet moment. - **Game guest links open again on a home network.** A guest link now uses the address the inviter reached this server by, instead of a developer address that opened nothing when the server's address was never set.
### 2026.11.12 — 4.87.0 The control panel, rearranged - **The control panel, rearranged.** Five groups instead of six — Infrastructure, Libraries & Scanning, Applications, Security & Members and System Settings — and the group you are in lists its pages down the side. Each application (Gallery, Videos, Ebooks, Audiobooks, Stories, Family Tree, Games) now keeps everything about it in one place, with a short row of tabs from **Overview**, **Device Sync**, **Organize** and **Settings**. Before, the panel sorted pages by kind, so Gallery’s duplicate cleanup sat under Maintenance, its maps under Settings and its phone backup under Library. Old bookmarks still land on the right page. - **A Dashboard that says what needs you.** It opens on what needs attention, each item with the page that fixes it; then the services beside this server with their addresses, the room left on each disk and how it has grown, how the server is used, and what it is doing now. - **Settings that read like a phone’s.** Nearly every settings page is now one column of grouped rows: each row says how it stands, and a row that leads somewhere opens a page of its own with Back. Switches and choices save the moment they change and numbers when you leave the field, so the Save buttons are gone — except on Email, where half-typed mail settings would break sending in between. Networks, blocked addresses, members, groups, invite links, quote packs, backups and scheduled jobs are lists you can open one by one, instead of wide tables with a row of buttons each. - **Turn a scheduled job on or off from the list.** Each job on **Scheduled jobs** has its switch on its row; the rest of the row opens it, with its schedule, when it last ran and what it reported, when it runs next, and **Run now**. - **Video settings, untangled.** **Applications › Videos › Settings** was one long page of four unrelated cards. It is now a short overview — converting video, the quality away from home (chosen right there), posters and descriptions, finding intros and credits (switch on the row) and copies for download — each opening a page with its explanation and settings, and every change saved as you make it. - **App access, a person at a time.** **Add a person or group** opens a search; whoever you pick starts as a member, and their row changes their role or removes them. Each thing an app does keeps its own “allowed from” choice. - **Phone backup in one place.** **Gallery › Device Sync** holds the phones, the networks they may back up from, the address they use and members’ personal libraries, each opening its own page. - **Help is one click away.** A **?** beside your name opens **Help & feedback**: the help guides and About iSputnik for everyone, and for administrators **Ask the community** (GitHub Discussions), **Report a bug** — the form already knows which version you run — and **Request a feature**. Before, help sat at the bottom of the menu under your name, where nobody looks for it. In the classic layout it is the sidebar’s **Help** item, and on a phone the end of the **Profile** tab. - **Orbit is the default theme.** Until an administrator picks a default, the sign-in screen and new accounts now start on Orbit, the iSputnik theme, instead of Minimalist. Accounts keep the theme they already have. - **The setup guide matches the control panel.** Its storage, Recycle Bin, backup, alert and email steps use the same rows as the pages they set.
### 2026.11.12 — 4.86.2 Stop preview, stopped - **Stop preview ends the preview.** On a server reached over HTTPS, **Stop preview** reloaded the page but left you looking at the app as the member, and even signing out and back in dropped you straight into the same preview — only clearing the browser’s site data got you out. The browser was quietly refusing the request to forget the preview. It now forgets it on Stop, on signing out, and whenever anyone signs in, so a fresh sign-in always starts as yourself. Thanks to Stefan Knol for the report and the recording (#102). - The same slip left sign-in, two-step and passkey cookies behind after they had served their purpose on HTTPS servers. They were already useless by then; they are now removed properly too.

Config.Name: Web UI Port
Config.Description: Port used to access the iSputnik web interface.

Config.Name: Config & Data
Config.Description: Stores database, metadata, thumbnails, backups, settings, and application data. Backups appear here under backups/.

Config.Name: Media Storage
Config.Description: Media storage path. Must be Read/Write — uploading photos/videos and filing them into dated folders writes here (scanning alone only needs read). Additional storage locations can be added later by editing the container or from within iSputnik.

Config.Name: PUID
Config.Description: User ID the app runs as. The server runs unprivileged (not root); on first start it takes ownership of the Config & Data path as this user. 99 (nobody) matches the default owner of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share is owned by a different user.

Config.Name: PGID
Config.Description: Group ID the app runs as. 100 (users) matches the default group of an Unraid appdata share — leave it unless your share uses a different group.

Config.Name: App URL
Config.Description: The address the app is reached at (for example https://isputnik.example.com). Set this when you put a reverse proxy or tunnel in front: it fixes the browser origin the app accepts, and an https address is also what turns on HTTPS-only enforcement (HSTS). Leave blank for plain LAN access.

Config.Name: HSTS
Config.Description: Leave blank. When App URL starts with https:// the app tells browsers to stay on HTTPS for a year. Set to false to suppress that — for example when your reverse proxy already sends its own Strict-Transport-Security header. Nothing is sent for a plain-http App URL either way.

Config.Name: Cookie Secure
Config.Description: Leave on auto: secure cookies then follow App URL — on when it starts with https://, off for a plain http home install. Set true or false only to override that. Secure cookies are never sent over plain http, so forcing true on an http install drops the sign-in cookie and you cannot log in. (auto needs version 1.13.3 or newer.)

Config.Name: Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a login session remains valid.

Config.Name: Linked Device Session Length (days)
Config.Description: Number of days a TV, wall display or other screen signed in with Link a device stays signed in. Each one is listed under Profile, Devices and can be revoked there.

Config.Name: Invite Validity (days)
Config.Description: Number of days invitation links remain valid.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Addresses
Config.Description: The reverse proxy's own IP or CIDR range, comma-separated for several (e.g. 172.18.0.0/16 for a Docker network). Preferred over Trusted Proxy Hops: forwarded headers are only believed when they come from these addresses. Leave blank for direct LAN access. Needed for correct per-IP rate limiting, auto-block, and trusted networks.

Config.Name: Trusted Proxy Hops
Config.Description: Alternative to Trusted Proxy Addresses when the proxy's IP isn't fixed: the number of reverse proxies in front of the app (usually 1 behind a reverse proxy or Cloudflare Tunnel). Leave blank for direct LAN access or when Trusted Proxy Addresses is set (addresses win if both are). Set it to match your proxy count, no higher, and don't expose the app's port directly.
